newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asia crude waits in limbo as traders eye October.
newsitem.headline: Asia crude waits in limbo as traders eye October.

text.p: Crude prices were fairly static in quiet trade in early Asia on Monday as buyers waited and assessed their Persian Gulf (PG) grade needs for October.
Brokers pegged notional cash Brent values for September at $18.90/18.90, flat against Friday levels.
Some slight firming was noted in October values, however, with cash Brent in the second month climbing 4 cents from Friday to $18.99/19.01.
"I wouldn't expect a start to Persian Gulf October trading until sometime later this week, as most Japanese refiners are still working on their programmes," said a trader with a French major.
"Things will be slow until then," he added.

In spot trade, a 400,000 barrel Bach Ho parcel was noted sold from a Japan trader to an Australian refiner at OSP plus 54 cents. The Japan refiner was reported to have purchased the material last week from a China trader at OSP plus 55. P. Lardner/Tokyo- 813-5473-3708 A. Ahmad/Singapore- 65-870-3086
